subject: Keeping sidebar always on the top of browser?

messages.author: 08e0e06fffa17b4d
messages.subject: Keeping sidebar always on the top of browser?
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if it's possible to show always the sidebar on the top browser even when scrolling down. I want this behavior because that I have a pretty long app with several plots on the same page, and I wouldn't like the user to scroll all the way up to change a parameter and then scroll down to see the results.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Keeping sidebar always on the top of browser?
parts:
Just define your own sidebarPanel with the affix class

sidebarPanel <- function (...) 
{
div(class = "span4", tags$form(class = "well affix", ...))
}


To test run

shiny::runGist("bb97d6764e3bd00c93f2")


ui.R

library(shiny)

sidebarPanel <- function (...) 
{
div(class = "span4", tags$form(class = "well affix", ...))
}

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  # Application title
  headerPanel("New Application"),
  
  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("obs", 
                "Number of observations:", 
                min = 1, 
                max = 1000, 
                value = 500)
  ),
  
  # Show a plot of the generated distribution
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot"),
    plotOutput("distPlot1"),
    plotOutput("distPlot2"),
    plotOutput("distPlot3"),
    plotOutput("distPlot4")
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
   
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
     
    # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
    # number of observations
    dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
    hist(dist)
    
  })
  
  output$distPlot1 <- renderPlot({
 
  # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
  # number of observations
  dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
  hist(dist)
 
  })
  
  output$distPlot2 <- renderPlot({
 
  # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
  # number of observations
  dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
  hist(dist)
 
  })
  
  output$distPlot3 <- renderPlot({
 
  # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
  # number of observations
  dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
  hist(dist)
 
  })
  
  output$distPlot4 <- renderPlot({
 
  # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
  # number of observations
  dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
  hist(dist)
 
  })
  
})
